caption: A 2x2 piston door that opens by itself: two rows of pressure plates on each side. Stepping on the row next to the door opens it; the outer rows give the door a memory. Once someone has stepped from an outer plate onto an inner one, the door stays open, even for someone standing still in the doorway where no plate can be, until they step off on an outer plate again. It works because plates of one kind let go in the order they were stepped on.

lock-v1 driven from the top: classic6's frame and dust, fed by a 3-torch tower beside the door, so one lock serves the whole door. The tower's top dust sits on a top slab: a full block there would hold the piston beside it on (no piston head above it to pass the update on), and the door would not open in two of the four rotations.

The smallest so far: lock-v3 with the tower's top torch hung on the tower, so it powers the block above it, which feeds the frame dust. The torch itself sits beside the near piston's frame and updates that piston when it turns off.

lock-v5 in a narrower box: the 3-torch tower stands one row off the door plane, diagonal to the pistons. Its top torch hangs beside the near piston's frame, and the far outer row's dust drops under the floor at the east side, where its climb back meets no other dust.
The smallest box: lock-v6 one level shorter. The far outer row's dust runs under the floor at y = -3, with two blocks above it beside the inner rows' dust so it cannot climb into them.

Robust to two people at any gap: lock-v7 with the outer plate rows four blocks out from the inner ones. The door now opens in 2 gt, and the lock waits 12 gt after the outer plates let go. The last inner plate always lets go, and the door has closed, before the lock can catch the door open, and a single person standing in the doorway is still caught open. A repeater halfway along the far row's long dust run keeps its signal alive.
lock-v8 with the lock torch's base beside the near outer row: the torch hangs on it, and the row's dust turns once to feed it through the 2 gt repeater. Two blocks fewer, the same timings.

Tripwire outer rows: tripwire re-checks every 10 gt where a plate re-checks every 20, so the rows can sit 3 blocks from the inner plates, with the lock at 18 gt. The right hooks' blocks feed the lock torch's base under the floor. Robust to two people at any gap, in a shorter box.
